items.title: An intersection of ideals is computed by an H1-regular sequence modulo an ideal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma computes an intersection of ideals under a regularity hypothesis: if the images of g_1 to g_m in A/I form an H_1-regular sequence, then I cap (g_1, ..., g_m) equals I times (g_1, ..., g_m) (statement lines 7471-7476). The proof is short but has real content (proof lines 7479-7494): it forms the standard short exact sequence of Koszul complexes attached to the surjection A to A/I, uses the vanishing of H_1 of the right hand complex, which is exactly the hypothesis, to read off injectivity of the induced map on the degree-one cokernels, and then identifies that injectivity statement with the asserted identity of ideals. The identification in the last step is where a reader has to work: the two cokernels are A^m to A and I^m to I, and their kernels are exactly (g_1, ..., g_m) and I(g_1, ..., g_m).
